hypothesis: Default locking is InMemoryLockingProvider, which only serializes within one process. The reservation path reads inventory_level.reserved_quantity, checks available_quantity, then writes back a computed reserved_quantity (read-modify-write, no row lock). With two servers on one database, two concurrent completions can both read the same reserved_quantity and both write back a stale total, so reserved_quantity may disagree with the live reservation rows, and possibly oversell. Test: two carts on different servers each holding OVS-PIECE (WIDGET stock 10), each with qty 6, so only one should succeed, completed together.

hypothesis: The availability check in ensureInventoryLevels compares available_quantity against item.quantity, where quantity is already multiplied by required_quantity in reserve-inventory. For OVS-TWOPACK (required_quantity 2) the check and the reservation should both use 2 per unit ordered. If the multiplication or the location choice is inconsistent between the check and the write, several two-pack orders could pass with only 10 WIDGET stocked. Test: several carts each buying 3 two-packs (6 WIDGET) against 10 stocked, completed together on one server.
